{{short description|American paleontologist}}'''K. Christopher Beard''' is an American [[paleontologist]], an [[expert]] on the [[primate]] [[Fossil|fossil record]] and a 2000 MacArthur Fellowship "Genius" Award Winner. Beard's [[research]] is reshaping critical [[Debate|debates]] about the evolutionary origins of [[Mammal|mammals]], including primates, routinely questioning current thinking about their geographical origins.<ref name=":0" /> Dr. Beard is the former Curator of the [[Carnegie Museum of Natural History]],<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.carnegiemnh.org/vp/cv/beard.htm |title=CMNH Vertebrate Paleontology: K. Christopher Beard |access-date=22 April 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100703023335/http://www.carnegiemnh.org/vp/cv/beard.htm |archive-date=3 July 2010 }}</ref> and Mary R. Dawson Chair of Vertebrate Paleontology, at [[University of Pittsburgh]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.geology.pitt.edu/people/adjunct.html|title = People &#124; Department of Geology and Environmental Science &#124; University of Pittsburgh &#124; University of Pittsburgh}}</ref> He is currently Distinguished Foundation Professor, Senior Curator at the [[University of Kansas]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://eeb.ku.edu/k-christopher-beard-named |title=K. Christopher Beard {{!}} Department of Ecology & Evolutionary Biology |website=eeb.ku.edu |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140522231501/https://eeb.ku.edu/k-christopher-beard-named |archive-date=22 May 2014}}</ref> He was co-author with Dan Gebo about an [[Extinction|extinct]] primate from [[China]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.niu.edu/pubaffairs/releases/2000/mar/primate/nature.htm |title=Newly discovered fossils from China shed light on common ancestry of monkeys, apes and humans |access-date=22 April 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100410013440/http://www.niu.edu/pubaffairs/RELEASES/2000/MAR/primate/Nature.htm |archive-date=10 April 2010 }}</ref> Dr. Beard also [[Author|authored]] the book ''The Hunt for the Dawn Monkey: Unearthing the Origins of Monkeys, Apes and Humans''.<ref name=":0">[http://www.carnegiemnh.org/science/default.aspx?id=17591 Science]</ref> Beard was also part of the research teams that discovered ''[[Teilhardina]]'', the earliest primate ever found in North America, and ''[[Eosimias]]'', one of the earliest higher primates yet discovered.<ref name=":0" /> He worked with [[NASA]] to scan a ''[[Tyrannosaurus rex]]'' skull.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nasa.gov/vision/earth/technologies/samson_skull.html|title=NASA - No Bones About It: NASA Analyzes Prehistoric Predator from the Past|access-date=22 April 2010|archive-date=18 March 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100318171442/http://www.nasa.gov/vision/earth/technologies/samson_skull.html}}</ref> Beard received his PhD from the Functional Anatomy and Evolution Program at [[Johns Hopkins School of Medicine|Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine]] in 1989.<ref name=":0" />
